source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 5: a and b such that u x v = 0 (book p.283). Answer key PDF 312: a = 21/5, b = 12/5.

blocks.prompt: 5. If the cross product of the vectors \(\underline{u} = 7\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{v} = a\underline{i} - b\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\) is zero, then find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).
blocks.explanation:
Cross product zero means the vectors are parallel.
We must find the unknowns \(a\) and \(b\).
Plan: compute \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) with letters, set every component to 0, solve, then use the third component as a check.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = 7\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = a\underline{i} - b\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \underline{0}\).
To find: \(a\) and \(b\).
Method: A vector is zero only when all three components are zero. So we write \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) by the determinant formula and equate each component to 0.

Write the determinant
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 7 & -4 & 5 \\ a & -b & 3 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 2 is \(\underline{u}\): \(7, -4, 5\). Row 3 is \(\underline{v}\): \(a, -b, 3\) (note the minus with \(b\)).

Work out the minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (-4)(3) - (5)(-b)\]
\[= -12 + 5b\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (7)(3) - (5)(a)\]
\[= 21 - 5a\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (7)(-b) - (-4)(a)\]
\[= -7b + 4a\]
Why: Cover the row and column of each unit vector; the letters are treated like numbers.

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = (5b - 12)\underline{i} - (21 - 5a)\underline{j}\]
\[+ (4a - 7b)\underline{k}\]
Why: The \(\underline{j}\) term is subtracted.

Set the components equal to zero
\[5b - 12 = 0 \Rightarrow b = \dfrac{12}{5}\]
\[21 - 5a = 0 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{21}{5}\]
Why: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \underline{0}\) means the \(\underline{i}\) and \(\underline{j}\) parts are 0.

Check with the \(\underline{k}\) component
\[4a - 7b = 4\left(\dfrac{21}{5}\right) - 7\left(\dfrac{12}{5}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{84}{5} - \dfrac{84}{5} = 0\]
Why: The third component must also vanish; it does.

Check another way
\[\dfrac{a}{7} = \dfrac{-b}{-4} = \dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \underline{0}\) means \(\underline{v} = \tfrac{3}{5}\underline{u}\) (parallel vectors), so \(a = \tfrac{3}{5}(7) = \tfrac{21}{5}\) and \(-b = \tfrac{3}{5}(-4)\), \(b = \tfrac{12}{5}\).
